# User requirements — Submission Readiness

**Document ID:** URS-SUBMISSION-READINESS
**Generated by:** `scripts/ops/generate-validation-package.mjs` from `docs/validation/launch/urs-registry.json`.
**Do not edit by hand — regenerate.** A hand edit is invisible to
`npm run ci:validation-traceability`, which is the only thing keeping the
citations below honest.

> **What this document is.** Qualification *evidence*, not a qualification. A
> qualification is a protocol executed and signed by a competent person; no
> script can be that. What this removes is the part a quality reviewer should
> never have to establish by hand — which requirement is implemented by which
> code, checked by which test, and whether that test actually ran and passed.
> Review starts from observed fact rather than from a claim.
>
> Every result below was observed at generation time. A verification that was
> not run reads NOT EXECUTED. A suite that could not start reads ERROR. Neither
> is ever rendered as a pass.

## Intended use

Whether a sequence may be dispatched, and, when it may not, exactly which requirement is unmet.

Surfaces in scope: `dispatch-readiness`, `orchestration`, `inconsistency`

**Reading the impact column.** `direct` means the software itself affects the
integrity, authenticity or content of a regulated record, or decides who may act
on one. `indirect` means it supports that work without producing the record.
The distinction sets the assurance effort: a direct-impact requirement cannot be
discharged by inspection, and the gate refuses a registry that tries.

## Requirement detail

### URS-SUBMISSIONREADINESS-90 — The system shall return a visitor with no session from the Submission Readiness surface `dispatch-readiness` to sign-in, and shall render that surface only once a session is established.

**Intended use.** A regulatory user reaches Submission Readiness through an authenticated session. The record this surface exposes is a regulated one, so an unauthenticated visitor must be returned to sign-in rather than shown any part of it.

**If it fails.** The surface renders for a visitor with no session, exposing a regulated record to an unidentified person and breaking the attribution every audit entry depends on.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** high

### URS-SUBRDY-01 — The system shall present the dispatch verdict for an eCTD sequence exactly as the server composed it, and shall treat a response that carries no verdict as unanswered rather than as cleared.

**Intended use.** A regulatory operations user opens Submission Readiness to learn whether a given eCTD sequence may be transmitted to the agency. The verdict is the product's safety claim about a regulated submission record, so it must be the one the server computed from tenant-scoped database state, never a number the browser re-derived.

**If it fails.** The surface recomputes the verdict from raw inputs using fewer gates than the server composes (it previously merged only two of four), so a sequence the server blocks renders as 'Cleared to dispatch' and publishes facts.cleared=true to the assistant. A regulator or sponsor would then believe a dossier had passed every pre-transmit control when the authoritative gate refused it.

**CSA impact.** indirect · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-SUBRDY-02 — The system shall refuse to clear a sequence for dispatch until at least one Shadow Review run has completed against it, and shall state that refusal as a named blocker.

**Intended use.** Prevents an adversarially-unreviewed dossier from being reported as fit to transmit. A reviewer uses the blocker list to know what must close before the sequence can leave the building.

**If it fails.** Zero open critical findings is read as 'clean' when it actually means 'nothing ever looked'. A sequence with no completed Shadow Review run clears the gate, and a dossier that was never adversarially reviewed is transmitted to the agency carrying a cleared verdict.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-SUBRDY-05 — The system shall block a production dispatch when an agency-grade external validator is required but could not be run or reported error-severity findings, and shall treat an unrecognised NODE_ENV as production for that rule.

**Intended use.** Where a sponsor licenses an external eValidator and enables the requirement, the platform must not allow a package to be dispatched on the strength of its own internal checks alone. Whether the rule is enforced must not depend on a misspelled environment variable.

**If it fails.** A misconfigured or unset NODE_ENV is treated as non-production, so the fail-closed rule silently switches off and a package the agency validator would have rejected is cleared and dispatched.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-SUBRDY-07 — The system shall not present a failed (non-2xx or unreachable) read of the approval-checkpoint store as zero pending approval gates — the Awaiting-approval count shall render as unread and the panel shall offer a control that re-issues the failed request; where the store is not provisioned the read route answers 200 with an empty set and meta.pendingStore, which this surface presently renders as zero.

**Intended use.** Honest failure behaviour on the Orchestration surface. A reviewer scanning the metrics strip for outstanding sign-offs must be able to tell 'none are pending' from 'we could not ask'.

**If it fails.** The checkpoints read fails, the mapped value stays an empty array, and the Awaiting-approval tile settles on 0. A reviewer who trusts it walks away from approval gates that are actually pending, and the surface's error copy tells them to retry with nothing on screen to retry with.

**CSA impact.** indirect · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-SUBRDY-09 — The system shall report the inconsistency submission gate as not assessed, and shall withhold every clearance statement, unless positive evidence exists that a contradiction assessment actually ran against the program.

**Intended use.** Clearance is a positive claim about a filing. The board persists detected contradictions and not the set of cross-references it verified, so absence of findings carries no information about whether anything was checked; the narrative must say so.

**If it fails.** A program the engine never scanned renders 'Submission gate — CLEAR' and 'no contradictions', because the empty-list branch and the nothing-found branch are the same expression. That is the most expensive sentence the surface can say to a regulatory director.

**CSA impact.** indirect · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-SUBRDY-10 — The system shall change a governed assumption's value only on receipt of a reason for change of at least eight characters, shall issue the replacement record and the supersession of the original within a single request and, if the supersession does not apply, shall refuse with an error naming the orphan replacement so it can be resolved, shall attempt best-effort (non-blocking) propagation marking downstream objects stale, and shall leave the stored value unchanged and say so when it refuses.

**Intended use.** Changing a governed assumption moves the dossier. The reason for change is what a reviewer reads to understand why, and the supersession chain is what makes the change auditable as one fact changing rather than two unrelated records.

**If it fails.** The two writes are issued separately and the second fails, leaving the old and new assumptions both live; or the client reports a change that was refused, so the user believes the dossier moved while the governed record still holds the previous value and nothing downstream was invalidated.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-SUBRDY-11 — The system shall reject a contradiction scan whose detector set did not run to completion, rather than returning the partial findings it did collect as a completed result.

**Intended use.** The Re-scan control on the inconsistency surface runs the real detection engine. A scan whose detectors crashed is an unknown result, and reporting it as a low finding count feeds a 'ready to promote' preflight verdict built on detectors that never executed.

**If it fails.** A detector catches its own read error, logs a warning and resolves with a partial array, so the response lists every detector as having run and returns a short total. A preflight verdict then reads 'zero blocking contradictions' for a dossier four detectors never examined.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium

### URS-SUBRDY-12 — The system shall verify that a workflow execution belongs to the caller's organization before cancelling it, shall perform that check before any cancellation takes effect, and shall answer not-found rather than forbidden for a run in another organization.

**Intended use.** The Cancel control on the Orchestration surface reaches a destructive route. Tenant isolation must hold on it as it does on the corresponding read, and the identifier space must not become an oracle that confirms another sponsor's run exists.

**If it fails.** Any authenticated user who knows an execution id cancels another sponsor's in-flight governed workflow, or learns from a 403 that the run exists. The other tenant's orchestration run is terminated with no trace of who did it in their organization's records.

**CSA impact.** direct · **assurance level achieved** medium
